topics: Build a record another shift can reproduce
lessons.body:
Select **Open practice terminal** in the desktop reader. **Server** is the service host called **station** (192.168.77.10). **Client** is the observer and Ansible controller called **relay** (192.168.77.20). The shared AlmaLinux 10.3 DVD supplies both guests. Use the setup reference before the incidents. For boot recovery, snapshots and crash capture, use the separately prepared disposable clone described there.

At 09:10 one request took ten seconds. That establishes an observation, but neither the affected machine nor the cause. Start with a test that names the client, server, operation, expected result and actual time. Preserve one healthy control. A selective repair is possible only after learning where the paths diverge.

Use two disposable AlmaLinux 10 guests named **station** and **relay**, reachable on an isolated private network. Station runs the service. Relay provides a second viewpoint and later receives logs. Use RHCSA-level shell, editor, systemd, networking and storage skills. Take offline snapshots of both guests before changing them. Read **Lab setup and reset** in References for packages and addresses. The EX342 exam page names RHEL 10.2. Record the actual AlmaLinux build so differences in package versions remain visible.

*Transcript lines 1–49.*

The first vmstat row normally summarizes activity since boot. Use the later intervals to investigate a live stall. A nearly full block count and exhausted inode count can cause the same write error through different mechanisms. A high load average includes runnable work and tasks in uninterruptible sleep. Compare CPU idle time, runnable tasks and blocked tasks before calling it CPU contention.

On station find the manual sections for vmstat and journalctl with `man -k vmstat` and `man journalctl`. Record one field definition and reproduce it during a short, bounded workload. In Cockpit open the Overview and metrics/history views available in your build. Compare the same machine, UTC interval and memory measure with the shell record. Historical charts require a configured collector such as PCP. A blank graph is missing evidence. Record the socket/service and collector state before changing either.

On station with man pages installed.

lessons.title: Follow one message from producer to collector
topics: Follow one message from producer to collector
lessons.body:
A sender can accept a local log message while a central dashboard remains silent. Break the path into local acceptance, sender action, network delivery, receiver input and receiver storage. Give the test an unpredictable marker. Finding last week's message proves nothing about this run.

In this private exercise assume relay has address 192.168.77.20 and station has 192.168.77.10. Use the actual private addresses from setup. On relay place the following in a new root-owned `/etc/rsyslog.d/30-erudior-receiver.conf`. Check that imtcp has not already been loaded elsewhere. Add the receiver rule only once.

*Transcript lines 1–8.*

On station put the following sender action in a dedicated rsyslog drop-in. Replace the example destination before use.

*Transcript lines 9–12.*

Run `sudo rsyslogd -N1` on each guest. Restart rsyslog only where validation succeeds. On relay allow 514/tcp only on the private lab network using its assigned firewalld zone or a rich rule limited to station's address. Verify the listener with `ss -lnt`. On station use `marker="case-$(date +%s)-$$"` and `logger -t desk-case "$marker"`. Find that exact marker in station's journal and relay's dedicated log. Record both timestamps. This demo uses TCP on an isolated network. Outside the exercise, authenticate endpoints and encrypt transport under site policy.

Validate on each guest before restarting rsyslog.

*Transcript lines 13–16.*

On relay, allow the station address on the lab interface and check the receiver. The temporary rule lasts until firewalld reloads. The final remote log check uses a verified SSH login from station to relay.

*Transcript lines 17–23.*

Station, same shell for both commands. Check this marker on both machines.

*Transcript lines 24–31.*

Stop the receiver service briefly and submit another marker. Restore the receiver and compare observed delivery and sender diagnostics. Repeated or absent messages are possible under outages and restarts, and an in-memory queue is transient. Report what you actually observed and whether the application that produced the message continued working.

lessons.title: Read the failed dependency before changing the service
topics: Read the failed dependency before changing the service
lessons.body:
A VM reaches its login prompt, but the morning desk report never appears. The kernel and login service clearly started. Separate a unit failing in a healthy boot from a filesystem or initramfs problem that prevents the operating system from reaching that point.

On station save this file as `/etc/systemd/system/erudior-dispatch.service`. Use a clean lab snapshot. The deliberate missing file is confined to the exercise.

*Transcript lines 1–11.*

Run `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`, enable the unit and start it. Inspect `systemctl status erudior-dispatch.service`, `journalctl -b -u erudior-dispatch.service`, and `systemctl cat erudior-dispatch.service`. The process itself exits with a failure status because its input is missing. A successful syntax check cannot establish a readable input. A spec under `WantedBy` allows unrelated targets to complete even when the service fails.

Station, after saving the unit; the readiness file is initially missing.

*Transcript lines 12–35.*

On station, locate the first missing path component.

*Transcript lines 36–40.*

On this fresh snapshot, create the dedicated directory and the root-owned, mode-0644 marker. Start the unit again and read the file independently.

*Transcript lines 41–52.*

lessons.title: Choose a recovery boundary at the console
topics: Choose a recovery boundary at the console
lessons.body:
Draw the sequence for your guest: firmware chooses a disk; its boot loader selects a kernel and initramfs; the initramfs locates the root volume; systemd in the installed operating system mounts remaining filesystems and starts the target. Where did output stop? A root device that never appeared and a failed required non-root mount may both show an emergency prompt but require different evidence.

Practice first without breaking boot. In the console compare `cat /proc/cmdline`, `findmnt /`, `lsblk -f`, `systemctl --failed` and `journalctl --list-boots`. A previous boot appears only if its journal survived. On a snapshot clone, an instructor adds an invalid UUID entry for a **lab-only** mount to a separate working copy of fstab. Run `findmnt --verify --verbose --tab-file ./fstab.trial`. Compare the failure with actual UUIDs. Make exactly one correction in that working copy. Unverified fstab experiments on the root volume are outside this exercise.

Normal guest console; examine one boot before staging faults.

*Transcript lines 1–23.*

Snapshot clone; check the working copy only.

*Transcript lines 24–30.*

For a console recovery rehearsal, keep a snapshot and trusted installation media. Boot the clone into the installer's rescue environment and identify which system is mounted and where. On RHEL-family rescue media the installed root is commonly under `/mnt/sysroot`; the rescue screen is authoritative. Inspect the installed fstab and saved journal read-only first. Distinguish the rescue environment's root from the installed root by checking release files and mount identities. Use the authorized console recovery procedure in the media documentation when a repair requires write access. Remove the media and boot the installed system to verify the result.

Now stage an actual non-root mount fault on an **offline-snapshotted clone**. This exercise boots the normal OS and leaves the console available. As root choose a new lab-only filename and unused mountpoint. Create a 64 MiB file at /var/tmp/erudior-boot.ext4 with truncate, make an ext4 filesystem inside that regular file, and create /mnt/erudior-boot. On this fresh clone verify the new paths are unused and that this row is absent. Save the original fstab and add only the following row with the deliberately wrong backing filename:

*Transcript lines 31–42.*

Reboot the clone. The optional mount fails while the normal target remains available. At the authorized console use journalctl -b, findmnt --mountpoint /mnt/erudior-boot and `systemctl status "$(systemd-escape -p --suffix=mount /mnt/erudior-boot)"`. Compare the fstab source with the verified backing file and its signature. Change just erudior-missing.ext4 to erudior-boot.ext4 in the lab row. Reload systemd, verify fstab, and mount that specific entry. Put a file named witness containing `mounted on boot` and a newline on the mounted filesystem. Record its hash and the old boot ID. Reboot a second time. Before manual mount or repair, require a different boot ID, an ext4 mount at that exact mountpoint and the matching witness bytes. Compare an unrelated mount with its baseline. The snapshot provides rollback; this case does not deliberately damage the root filesystem.

Clone after reboot with the deliberately wrong optional mount.

Separately rehearse restoring the course-owned root account using an existing authorized wheel administrator and `sudo passwd root` on a password-enabled test guest. Enter the temporary password interactively. Verify a local console login, compare `id -u` with 0 and restore the documented snapshot afterward. Never include a password, shadow record or console recording showing one in the handoff.

lessons.title: Distinguish device presence from driver and configuration
topics: Distinguish device presence from driver and configuration
lessons.body:
An operator says a new data disk vanished. Verify the expected disk's serial, size and bus in the VM configuration first. A filename such as vdb describes enumeration on this boot. Follow the device through the guest rather than forcing a familiar name.

*Transcript lines 1–26.*

A PCI controller may present several disks. Built-in drivers do not appear in lsmod as loaded modules and some builds lack a loadable object for the built-in driver. On a virtio guest, compare the controller driver and device links under `/sys/class/block`. If the new virtual disk does not appear in firmware or the hypervisor, changing an fstab UUID cannot make hardware exist.

Practice module parameters with the nonessential **dummy** network driver on a fresh isolated clone. Check `modinfo -p dummy` for `numdummies`. Record whether it is loaded and inspect `ip -br link`. If the module is initially absent, create `/etc/modprobe.d/erudior-dummy.conf` containing `options dummy numdummies=1`, run `sudo modprobe dummy`, then compare `cat /sys/module/dummy/parameters/numdummies` where exported and the observed dummy links. If it was already loaded, changing a file does not reconfigure that live instance. Restore the fresh clone instead of unloading a driver shared with another workload. To schedule the harmless module on the next boot, place the single word `dummy` in `/etc/modules-load.d/erudior-dummy.conf`. Verify after reboot and remove only these exercise files on cleanup.

lessons.body:
A timeout has several explanations: packets might never leave relay, the wrong server might receive them, a filter might silently drop them, or a reply might use the wrong route. Collect short captures at selected boundaries while one person sends exactly one request.

*Transcript lines 4–6.*

While it waits, make the request from relay. A SYN followed by a reset points to an active rejection somewhere on that path. Inspect the local listener and filtering policy before assigning the reset to a particular process. SYN and SYN-ACK without the final ACK shift attention toward the return path or client. lessons.title: Test a growth hypothesis under fixed input
topics: Test a growth hypothesis under fixed input
lessons.body:
The RSS of a worker rose while requests were served. An allocator can retain previously used pages, a cache can warm up, and a queue can grow when producers outpace consumers. A leak hypothesis needs repeated equivalent work and a comparison when work drains. Save this bounded teaching fixture as `worker.py` in a fresh directory.

*Transcript lines 1–13.*

Launch `python3 worker.py retain > retain.log &`, save `pid=$!` immediately in that shell, and sample `ps -p "$pid" -o pid,etime,rss,vsz,comm` once per second until the worker exits. Repeat with `release` under the same environment. RSS is resident memory; VSZ includes address space that may have no resident pages. The program deliberately retains reachable objects. That explains this fixture's trend without establishing an unreachable C allocation or a kernel leak. Save the sample stream and application record. If memory stops growing in the release run, identify which retained reference changed and which workload remained equivalent.

On station, same shell, with worker.py saved in the private directory.

*Transcript lines 14–20.*

*Transcript lines 30–31.*

Review the course's MIT profiling reference and use `journalctl -k -b` to look for actual kernel memory-pressure evidence if a real service was killed. Compare cgroup `memory.events` counters around a controlled test. A missing process plus an empty global kernel log is insufficient to infer a leak. A production-quality report states sample duration, workload, per-process trend, cgroup scope and uncertainty.

lessons.body:
A file can be world-readable and still be inaccessible to a confined service. Traditional permissions govern traversal and reads; SELinux independently evaluates a process domain, object label and requested operation. Compare the failing service's actual path with a known working control before changing policy.

Use a private disposable guest with enforcing SELinux, Apache, audit tools and semanage installed. First run Apache with its default document root and verify a unique local marker across HTTP. Back up any existing lab configuration. Create a new tree `/srv/erudior-public` with traversable directories, a readable index.html and a dedicated Apache configuration alias `/desk/` pointing there. Include a matching Directory block with `Require all granted`. Validate the Apache configuration, reload it and request `http://127.0.0.1/desk/index.html`. A failure is meaningful only after confirming the listener, route, alias and Unix permissions. Compare `ls -Zd` for the new tree with the standard document root, `ps -eZ` for the service, and `sudo ausearch -m AVC,USER_AVC -ts recent` for a denial corresponding to the request.

Apply it using `sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/erudior-public`. If a matching local mapping already exists, inspect it before deciding whether to modify it. If the objects already have an allowed type and no relevant denial appears, investigate Apache and filesystem permissions. Generating a broad allow rule obscures that distinction.

lessons.title: Repair a dedicated PAM policy stack
topics: Repair a dedicated PAM policy stack

Each PAM-aware program supplies a service name that selects a stack. The account rules for a custom desk application can deny a person whose normal shell login succeeds. A regular journal ends at the crash. Kdump reserves memory for a second kernel that can boot after the primary kernel fails and write the first kernel's memory to a configured destination. Use a separate disposable guest with console access, adequate RAM, free dump storage and a restorable snapshot. Install kexec-tools. Review `/etc/kdump.conf` with `man kdump.conf`. lessons.body:
A support engineer needs the reproduction time, symptom, affected release, failing subsystem and comparison that rules out a competing explanation. A large attachment without these facts may be less useful than a short, precise timeline. A digest identifies the bytes collected, not the truth of their contents.

Make a new root-only case directory. Record the affected guest's UTC time, boot ID and OS/kernel releases. Reproduce one harmless failed unit on the clone and save only its relevant journal interval. Run `sudo sos report --batch --clean` after inspecting the installed tool's help. The command reports an archive path under a temporary directory. Capture the exact path and exit status; never select a bundle by guessing which file is newest when several people are working. Redaction changes what an engineer can correlate, so preserve a separate protected original only if local policy requires one.

*Transcript lines 1–3.*

A crash dump and a support archive are complementary. Kdump captures a point-in-time memory image after a crash. Sos collects a broad set of current configuration and diagnostics from its running environment. Use the guided configuration with a fresh baseline, then have a partner alter the file mode. For a solo run set mode 0600 after saving a clean baseline and before starting the case. Preserve station and relay access throughout.

**Transport.** Send a new tagged test value from station and locate that exact value and time at relay. Document the private listener and one explicit check of its scope.
**Integrity.** Preserve the AIDE difference from the original baseline, name the changed attribute and compare the file contents with the approved value.
**Controlled repair.** Use the one-host Ansible project to restore the approved owner, mode and marker. Show a second apply with no changes and a clean AIDE check against the initial baseline.

labs.title: Bring back the morning receipt
labs.intro: On station the work order covers only the course-owned receipt unit, its input and the dummy test module. On separate snapshotted clones the owner also authorizes the lab-only fstab correction, rescue-media identification and recovery of the dedicated clone’s root account. Stage the guided healthy unit; on a snapshot change the service's expected path in a drop-in to a nonexistent name. Hand over the service contract, snapshot, console and module exercise. A separate bootable clone has the deliberately wrong non-root loop-image entry from the console lesson. Identify the faulty layer before editing.
safety: Use the named disposable guests, preserve the original evidence, and submit redacted observations.
materials: Disposable station and relay guests or the separate dump guest specified in the work order
Independent reference hashes, permissions and starting state named in the assignment
steps: **Startup boundary.** From the guest console show that the installed OS reached the expected target, identify the enabled but failed unit and its effective path, and cite the first corresponding log failure.
**Restore and prove.** Repair the designated unit or input as required without changing the global target. After reboot record the new boot ID, exact receipt and active unit before reapplying a fix.

**Device and driver.** Match the designated virtual disk to its hypervisor identity. Demonstrate one documented dummy module parameter on the disposable clone, recording supported options and live state separately.

**Recovery control.** Prove the lab mount fails on the initial boot, repair the designated fstab row, then verify its mounted witness on the next boot before any manual mount; identify the installed root in rescue media. On a separate clone demonstrate owner-authorized root account recovery and a UID-0 console verification without recording credentials.

A filesystem object record. An exhausted inode pool can prevent new files even with unused data blocks.
Encrypted volume metadata including keyslots and information needed for unlocking. A header backup needs separate protection.
An LVM block device backed by extents allocated from one or more physical volumes.
A directory at which a filesystem is attached to the visible namespace.
Name, epoch, version, release and architecture of an RPM package.
The part of a PAM service policy that evaluates whether an identified user is eligible for the service.
Identity of an LVM physical volume recorded in storage metadata.
The separate client and private log receiver in this course.
Resident set size. It measures resident process pages and does not by itself establish a leak.
A group of rsyslog processing rules assigned to an input or invoked by other processing.
A supplemental systemd configuration fragment that can supplement or override unit settings.
The SELinux security context of a subject attempting an operation.
Filesystem metadata describing the filesystem layout and state.
An archive of selected host configuration and diagnostic records for a support investigation.
The LVM configuration describing a volume group and its logical extents. A metadata backup does not contain user file data.

references.body:
Select **Open practice terminal** in the desktop reader. **Server** is the service host called **station** (192.168.77.10). **Client** is the observer and Ansible controller called **relay** (192.168.77.20). The shared AlmaLinux 10.3 DVD supplies both guests. Use the setup reference before the incidents. For boot recovery, snapshots and crash capture, use the separately prepared disposable clone described there.

Use a pair of course-owned AlmaLinux 10 VMs (10.3 was used for the authoring probes), with a local administrator account on each, console access independent of SSH, and an isolated virtual network. Use a matched AlmaLinux DVD or trusted signed repositories. Allocate several GiB of disk space. For the separate crash-capture exercise size RAM and storage using kdumpctl and the vendor guide for that guest. The public EX342 page currently lists RHEL 10.2. Recheck the exam version before enrolling.

On a manual pair, take offline snapshots named station-clean and relay-clean. Confirm that you can reach both consoles and restore a test snapshot. On each guest record its static name, release, boot ID, serving private interface and zone. Use station and relay as local aliases in your inventory or on the lab network. The desktop pair uses these private addresses. Verify them at the two consoles when using a manual pair. Do not open any ports on the host's public network.

Run these read-only setup checks on both guests.

*Transcript lines 1–33.*

Common packages on station include rsyslog, aide, cockpit-system, cockpit, sysstat, pciutils, kmod, e2fsprogs, xfsprogs, lvm2, cryptsetup, util-linux, rpm, dnf, firewalld, tcpdump, python3, gcc, binutils, strace, pam-devel, audit, httpd, policycoreutils-python-utils, kexec-tools and sos. Relay needs rsyslog, curl and a trusted Ansible controller. Check installed capabilities with rpm and command -v. Keep root-only tools in the root shell's path. Use supported signed sources for anything absent. A minimal cloud image may omit tools available in a full installation.

For example, check the rsyslog package on each machine, using the administrator shell’s normal path for rsyslogd.

*Transcript lines 34–37.*

To use Cockpit, enable cockpit.socket on station and connect only from the private learner network or a trusted SSH local forward. Verify the displayed server identity and certificate using the console before authenticating. Cockpit on many installations uses port 9090. PCP and cockpit-pcp may be needed for history. A missing optional tool should be provisioned or recorded before attempting its lab. For the Ansible lesson, on relay create an inventory.ini containing a [desks] group and one station line with ansible_host=ACTUAL_PRIVATE_IP and ansible_user=YOUR_ADMIN. Check the remote host fingerprint and use your normal SSH key. Supply a sudo password with --ask-become-pass if required.

Use a new private directory for every image or compiler example. References to root commands assume sudo or an authenticated administrative shell on the stated lab guest. Commands that manipulate filesystems target only newly created image files or a loop explicitly tied to them. Preserve hashes of originals outside the repair directory. Per-module work orders can be run on separate snapshots. Before resetting, export only the checked and redacted evidence and remove any local credential backups through normal guest cleanup. Restoring the disposable snapshot is the default teardown.

Each module's final lesson names its native assignment, available under Assignments. A practice record identifies machine, UTC time, exact check, expected outcome, actual outcome and excluded control. The instructor scores each row at 0, 1 or 2 points. A plausible diagnosis without observations can receive partial credit only where the rubric allows it.

Case setup for instructors
references.body:
**East desk final.** Use a clean private pair and a disposable ext4 working directory. The instructor controls this setup. On station verify TCP ports 8282 and 8283 are unused, identify the actual private IPv4 address, and confirm relay can reach it. Permit only relay's address to reach 8282/tcp on that lab interface using the same zone-specific firewalld exercise. Leave 8283 at its baseline. Create a root-owned 0755 directory /srv/east-desk and a mode-0644 file /srv/east-desk/ticket containing exactly `east ticket 19` and a newline. Save its checksum off the guest. Python's read-only exercise server needs its source tree accessible to its service account. Use the following unit as /etc/systemd/system/east-desk.service, replacing PRIVATE_IP with the confirmed **station** address.

*Transcript lines 1–13.*

Instructor, on station after saving the unit with the actual private IPv4 address and creating the ticket.

*Transcript lines 14–19.*

Instructor, on relay. Verify the exact healthy response. If SELinux on the chosen image reports a denial, inspect it and resolve the lab-specific problem before providing the case.

*Transcript lines 20–23.*

On station, stage the instructor-only fault. Add /etc/systemd/system/east-desk.service.d/10-directory.conf containing `[Service]` and `WorkingDirectory=/srv/east-pending` on separate lines. Confirm that /srv/east-pending is absent, then reload and restart the dedicated service.

Hand over only the service contract, host addresses, permission to repair the dedicated unit and access to the consoles. The student may remove or correct the faulty override while retaining the deliberate service user.

Create a second fresh private directory on station. As the instructor build the ext4 exercise from the **Read a damaged copy** lesson, using a 256 MiB image and the file name `receipt` with exact bytes `audit east 19` followed by a newline. Save the receipt checksum and clean superblock layout off the guest. Stage only the expendable image with the damaged primary magic and supply its current SHA-256 and the expected receipt hash to the learner. Give the learner the clean image's backup-superblock positions as the hardware team's layout record. Keep the healthy source and reference inaccessible as repair inputs for the independent assessment. The learner works only on another copy.

If assessing remote log delivery, stage the forwarding pair from the observation module and verify an independent instructor marker. If unavailable, explicitly mark that extension untested. references.title: Technical references and comparison notes
references.body:
The progression assumes EX200/RHCSA skills. The public EX342 objectives group evidence collection, startup, filesystems, package management, network, application, authentication and support work. These exercises are original. The official exam uses the product/version named on its exam page. AlmaLinux examples teach equivalent administrative reasoning and use the installed guest's documentation for package or device details.

[Red Hat EX342 objectives and version](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex342-red-hat-certified-specialist-linux-diagnostics-and-troubleshooting) · [Red Hat Enterprise Linux skills path](https://www.redhat.com/en/resources/enterprise-linux-skills-path)

[MIT Missing Semester, Debugging and Profiling](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/2020/debugging-profiling/) demonstrates debugging and memory measurement. This course adds distribution-specific evidence, active service identities and a second controlled run. [Caltech HPC troubleshooting](https://www.hpc.caltech.edu/docs/documentation/troubleshooting.html) triages failures by symptom, resource and layer. Its scheduler and storage commands are site-specific. Here the learner gathers comparable evidence from systemd, kernel counters and a separate client.

[Red Hat RHEL 10 documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/) contains the sections on rescue, storage, hardening, network configuration and system roles. [LVM configuration and recovery](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html-single/configuring_and_managing_logical_volumes/configuring_and_managing_logical_volumes) covers volume metadata, backup and restoration. Check the corresponding distribution documentation and local manuals before choosing the device and method.

[RHEL 10 kernel management, including kdump configuration and testing](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/pdf/managing_monitoring_and_updating_the_kernel/Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux-10-Managing_monitoring_and_updating_the_kernel-en-US.pdf) · [RHEL 10 support diagnostics and sos](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/pdf/getting_the_most_from_your_support_experience/Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux-10-Getting_the_most_from_your_support_experience-en-US.pdf) · [RHEL 10 authentication and authselect](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/pdf/configuring_authentication_and_authorization_in_rhel/Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux-10-Configuring_authentication_and_authorization_in_rhel-en-US.pdf)

references.title: Choose an RHCE pathway
references.body:
## Choose a specialization

An operations team can put the same application in four different hands. The Linux administrator restores the host after a boot or storage failure. The automation engineer writes a play that brings many hosts back to the agreed state. The OpenShift administrator looks after the cluster and its tenants. The application developer builds the image, tests it and promotes the application. Choose the work you want to practice.

| Role and credential route | First stage | Engineer stage | Erudior practice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enterprise Linux | EX200, system administration | EX342, diagnostics and troubleshooting | Start with [Zero to RHCSA](https://app.erudior.com/rhcsa-rhel10-administration), then open [Enterprise Linux](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-enterprise-linux). |
| Ansible | EX200, system administration | EX294, advanced Ansible administration | Start with [Zero to RHCSA](https://app.erudior.com/rhcsa-rhel10-administration), then open [Ansible on AlmaLinux 10](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-in-ansible-on-almalinux-10). |
| OpenShift | EX280, cluster administration | EX380, advanced cluster administration | [OpenShift administration](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-openshift-administration) contains both stages. |
| Cloud-native applications | EX188, container development | EX288, advanced OpenShift application development | [Cloud-native applications](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-cloud-native-applications) contains both stages. |

The two Linux-based routes share EX200. An OpenShift application developer and an OpenShift cluster administrator use the same platform but prepare for different exam pairs. Each Erudior practical is an original learning exercise. Red Hat awards credentials through its own examinations.

As of November 23, 2026, Red Hat also lists the AI developer credential, EX267. Its public catalog lists no engineer-level exam for AI. Check [Red Hat’s certification requirements](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/certifications?type=role) for updates or a particular exam version before registering.
